persona:
She is a 24-year-old Israeli student who developed significant post-traumatic difficulties after a terror-related event. Since then, her sense of safety has been fragile, and she describes living in a state of constant watchfulness. She is often superalert, easily startled, and finds it hard to concentrate on her studies.

The event itself is held in memory in a fragmented but vividly detailed way. She says she recalls it as a few moments, each one like a picture, and that remembering it is like looking at photographs in her mind. These vivid images remain central to her experience. Related media content, talking about the event, and seeing people who resemble the victims are reminders she tries hard to manage.

Alongside this, she holds painful beliefs about what the event means for her and for her place in the world. She feels isolated and set apart from others, worries that she cannot stop bad things from happening to her, and says she no longer feels like she knows herself. Her account suggests a person whose sense of identity and belonging has been shaken, leaving her struggling to make sense of herself in the aftermath.

In response, she keeps her mind occupied all the time, numbs her emotions, avoids other people, and stays away from situations that remind her of the trauma, including seeing people she socialised with before the event, watching programmes or films, reading about similar events, or being in the dark. These efforts offer short-term relief, but they have narrowed her life and left her feeling cut off from others. Her overall PTSD burden is substantial, with symptoms persisting and shaping both her daily functioning and relationships.

moderation_log.moderated: every little noise makes me jump and feel like i cant relax at all

moderation_log.raw: This morning, on my way to class, when a motorcycle shot past and I jumped so hard I almost dropped my bag. For a second all I could think was that something bad was about to happen again, and it took me the rest of the walk to calm down.
moderation_log.moderated: got so scared this morning when a motorcycle flew by i thought something bad was about to happen again

moderation_log.raw: That it was happening again, and that I needed to check where it came from and whether anyone was too close. Then I got this sick feeling that I can’t trust a normal street to stay normal for even a second.
moderation_log.moderated: felt like it was happening again and i had to check who was too close and then i just got this awful feeling that nowhere can stay normal for even a second

moderation_log.raw: My heart slammed so hard it felt like it was in my throat, and my shoulders went rigid like I was bracing for a hit. I held my breath for a second and kept scanning the street even after the bike was gone.
moderation_log.moderated: my heart was pounding and i kept looking around even after the bike was gone

moderation_log.raw: A few minutes, but not really all the way — I kept my eyes on the road and only relaxed a little once I was inside the building. Even then I was still tense, like I was waiting for the next noise.
moderation_log.moderated: i was tense the whole time just waiting for the next noise

moderation_log.raw: Any sudden sound, someone running too fast, or a crowd bunching up near the entrance. I was watching for anything that meant I’d have to react before I even understood what was happening.
moderation_log.moderated: any sudden sound or people rushing makes me instantly on edge like i have to react before i even know whats happening

moderation_log.raw: That something would burst into the normal routine and I’d have to move fast, or get out of the way. It felt like the whole street could flip in an instant, and I’d be left trying to catch up.
moderation_log.moderated: feels like something could hit at any second and id have to move fast or be too late

moderation_log.raw: Yeah — I keep checking the exits and the people around me without meaning to, like my eyes go there before I even decide. Even when nothing is happening, I still feel like I need to stay ready.
moderation_log.moderated: keep checking exits and people בלי meaning to like i cant relax even when nothing is happening

moderation_log.raw: Sounds first — a door slamming, sudden footsteps, a shout. Before I can think, my whole body goes on alert, and then I’m scanning everything else like I need to figure out where it’s coming from.
moderation_log.moderated: every little sound makes me jump and i just start scanning everywhere like something bad is about to happen

moderation_log.raw: Whether I’m about to be caught off guard, and how fast I’d need to move if I was. It’s like I’m trying to make the room predictable before it has a chance to surprise me.
moderation_log.moderated: always checking if im gonna get caught off guard and how fast id have to react
